extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline; Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order approving a settlement imposing public discipline (a 60‑day suspension) on a registered USPTO practitioner, setting forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions under USPTO rules, required compliance steps during suspension, affidavit and publication requirements, and reinstatement eligibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent ... has been an attorney registered to practice before the USPTO ... and subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, which are set forth at 37 CFR §§ 11.101 through 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners are governed by the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 CFR §§11.101–11.901); those rules provide the substantive standards for professional behavior and discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction over disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 CFR §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary proceedings involving registered practitioners proceed under statutes (35 U.S.C.) and implementing regulations (37 CFR §§11.19, 11.20, 11.26).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition/discipline for being publicly disciplined by a State (37 CFR §11.804(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the information contained in the Joint Stipulated Facts above, [Respondent] violated the following provision of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct: 37 CFR § 11.804(h)(1) (being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State) by being disciplined on professional misconduct grounds by the Supreme Court of the State of Oregon on June 13, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public disciplinary action by a state authority can constitute a violation of USPTO professional conduct rules and trigger USPTO sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction imposed: suspension length and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be suspended nunc pro tunc from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for a period of sixty (60) days commencing on October 5, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies the duration (60 days), retroactive effective date (nunc pro tunc to Oct 5, 2022), and scope (patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters) of the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cease practice and representation during suspension (37 CFR §11.58(b)(1) & (c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent represents that on July 22, 2022, he ceased all activities related to practice before the Office and ceased representing clients pursuant to 37 CFR §§ 11.58(b)(1) and (c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During suspension a practitioner must stop all activities before the USPTO and must not represent clients in matters before the Office until reinstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cease holding out as authorized to practice (37 CFR §11.58(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent represents that on July 22, 2022, he ceased holding himself out as authorized or able to practice before the USPTO pursuant to 37 CFR § 11.58(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners under suspension must stop any communication or representation that would reasonably suggest they are authorized to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove advertisements and representations (37 CFR §11.58(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent represents that, pursuant to 37 CFR § 11.58(b)(3), he has taken all necessary steps to remove any advertisements or other representations that would reasonably suggest he is authorized or able to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspended practitioners must remove or correct advertising, websites, letterhead, directories, and other representations implying USPTO practice eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of compliance and required attachments (37 CFR §11.58(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within ten (10) days of the date of this Final Order, Respondent shall provide an affidavit of compliance in accordance with 37 CFR § 11.58(d) certifying that he has complied with the provisions of the Agreement. Appended to the affidavit shall be: (1) a copy of each form of notice, the names and addresses to which notices were sent, and all return receipts or returned mail received up to the date of the affidavit, as set forth in 37 CFR § 11.58(d)(1); (2) a list of all state, federal, and administrative jurisdictions to which Practitioner is admitted to practice; and (3) a description of the steps taken by Practitioner to remove any advertisements or other representations that would reasonably suggest that the practitioner is authorized to practice patent, trademark, or other non-patent law before the Office, as set forth in 37 CFR § 11.58(d)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit is a formal certification of compliance with suspension requirements and must include documentary evidence of notices, a jurisdictions list, and an account of steps taken to remove misleading representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations regarding clients, files, and fees during suspension (37 CFR §11.58(c)(3)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent represents that he has no clients, possesses no client papers or other property, and retains no unearned fees or unexpended advanced costs as set forth in 37 CFR § 11.58(c)(3). Respondent represents that he has no matters involving opposing practitioners or parties as set forth in 37 CFR § 11.58(c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must safeguard client property and fees; during suspension they must account for client files, avoid conflicts with opposing practitioners, and not retain unearned fees—if clients exist, specified notification and transfer/closing steps under 11.58 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on resuming practice until reinstated (37 CFR §11.60(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not resume practice of patent, trademark, or other non-patent law before the Office until reinstated by order of the OED Director or the USPTO Director as set forth in 37 CFR § 11.60(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires an order of the OED or USPTO Director; automatic resumption of practice is not permitted upon passage of time alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement eligibility timing (continuous compliance period equal to suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not be eligible for reinstatement until a continuous period of the time in compliance with 37 CFR § 11.58 that is equal to the period of suspension or exclusion has elapsed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility for reinstatement requires a continuous period of compliance (i.e., being out of practice and meeting 11.58 obligations) equal to the length of the suspension before applying for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish this Final Order at OED’s electronic FOIA Reading Room ... The OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the following: [Notice of Suspension template].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary Final Orders are publicly posted and a standard Official Gazette notice is published summarizing the facts, findings, sanction, and information about submission of information relevant to reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations taken into account in imposing sanction (mitigating factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: In reaching this settlement, the OED Director considered that Mr. Duncan has (1) accepted responsibility for his actions; (2) expressed contrition and understands the seriousness of his actions and how his actions violated the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct; (3) not been previously publicly disciplined; and (4) provided full and fair disclosures to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline during the investigation of this matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of responsibility, contrition, lack of prior public discipline, and cooperation/ full disclosures are mitigating factors considered in determining discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of procedural review and appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent has waived the opportunity: (i) to seek reconsideration of this Final Order under 37 CFR §11.56, (ii) to have this Final Order reviewed under 37 CFR § 11.57, and (iii) otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements may include an explicit waiver of rights to reconsideration, review, or appeal of the Final Order under applicable CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation of right to pursue further discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Final Order shall prevent the Office from seeking discipline against Respondent for any other misconduct engaged in by Respondent prior to, during, or after his period of suspension;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement and imposed sanction do not bar the USPTO from initiating separate disciplinary proceedings for other misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order can specify that each party bears its own costs rather than awarding costs to either side.

rubrics_metrics.name: State conviction and misconduct findings as grounds for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: On March 19, 2020, Respondent unlawfully and knowingly offered and agreed to pay a fee to engage in sexual conduct ... On December 21, 2020 ... Respondent pleaded guilty to one count of violating ORS 167.008, a misdemeanor ... On June 13, 2022, a trial panel of the Supreme Court of the State of Oregon determined that Respondent’s conviction ... violated ORS 9.527(2) (commission of a misdemeanor crime involving moral turpitude). The panel also determined Respondent violated Rule 8.4(a)(3) of the Oregon Rules of Professional Conduct (misrepresentation and dishonesty reflecting adversely on fitness to practice law) by engaging in acts of misrepresentation with law enforcement during the investigation ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal convictions (including misdemeanors involving moral turpitude) and state disciplinary findings of dishonesty or misrepresentation can serve as bases for USPTO disciplinary action.
